name: Counterfactual / off-policy learning of when to override a default decision - CRM and BanditNet, doubly-robust policy learning, SelectiveNet, learning to defer

inputs_state_output: Authors' setups (all are generic decision/learning frameworks, none is a tracker except P12/P13): (a) CRM/BanditNet/DR (P1-P5): input context x, a logged action y ~ pi0(.|x) with known (or estimated) propensity, and a loss/reward observed ONLY for the logged action (bandit feedback); no internal memory; output is a stochastic policy pi_w(y|x) (softmax/exponential model, ResNet20 in P3; trees in P5). (b) SelectiveNet (P6): input x, shared body, three heads: prediction f(x), selection g(x) in [0,1] (sigmoid), auxiliary h(x); output = f(x) if g(x)>=tau else abstain. (c) Learning to defer (P8-P10): input x, a fixed external expert decision m (here: the default), output K class logits plus one deferral logit g_perp; defer iff max_y g_y <= g_perp. (d) P12 tracker: state = appearance model + heatmap + current frame (a recurrent belief), Q-network on the heatmap outputs Q for TRACK/REINIT and UPDATE/IGNORE. Ours: bounded grey crop into FlyVis whose recurrent state runs over 4 exemplar + search frames; per query a variable set of n real detection regions each with 68 pooled regional activity features, an observed-target descriptor (ridge target model), 8 geometry inputs and 6 assignment-context features; output = one score per region (plus implicit default). Key structural difference: our logged data is FULL-INFORMATION per step (good/harm label for EVERY candidate region vs the baseline assignment, computed by exact one-step re-assignment), whereas CRM/BanditNet/DR are designed for PARTIAL (bandit) feedback. Our setting is therefore cost-sensitive multiclass classification with a distinguished zero-cost default class, exactly the reduction used in P8 (eq. 4), not an off-policy problem at the single-step level. It becomes off-policy only across time: labels are one-step outcomes under the baseline's roll-in (states the baseline tracker visited), while the learned policy, once it acts, visits different states (P16, P12).
action_and_refusal: CRM/BanditNet: no explicit abstain; 'keep the default' corresponds to the logging policy's action, and the translation constant lambda in BanditNet plays the role of a baseline value (losses delta_i - lambda); with lambda wrong the learner systematically avoids or prefers logged actions (propensity overfitting). DR policy learning (P5): treatment assignment pi(x) in {control, treatments}; control is an ordinary arm whose value is subtracted (advantage scores Gamma_i(a) - Gamma_i(0)); act iff the estimated advantage of the chosen arm, as judged by the policy class, is positive. SelectiveNet: abstention is a separate sigmoid head g(x) with target coverage c enforced by a quadratic penalty, threshold re-calibrated post hoc to a coverage quantile. Learning to defer (P8): deferral to the expert is an extra class with its own LEARNED logit g_perp in a single softmax; defer iff g_perp >= max_y g_y (no extra threshold needed for consistency). P12: IGNORE (no update) and TRACK are the default branches; Q-values compared directly (argmax). Ours: transfer the full XYWH box of the selected region into the track state before native ByteTrack matching; default = fixed logit 0; rule (tracking/z13_region_assignment.py apply_policy): act on k=argmax z only if z_k>0 AND softmax probability exp(z_k)/(1+sum_j exp(z_j)) >= tau, tau from a grid {0,...,0.9,1.01} chosen on fit20. Note: fixing the default logit at 0 is by itself harmless (softmax is shift-invariant, so P8's model with a learned g_perp can be reparametrised with g_perp=0). What differs from P8 is (i) our z are trained by MSE regression, not by a softmax/cross-entropy surrogate, so exp(z) has no probability meaning, and (ii) the extra probability threshold makes the decision depend on n and on the other candidates' scores (see labels_and_loss).
labels_and_loss: P1 CRM: minimise clipped IPS risk + lambda*sqrt(Var/n) (variance regularisation = pessimism toward poorly-supported actions). P2/P3: self-normalised IPS (SNIPS), equivariant to loss translation; because SNIPS has no unbiased per-sample gradient, BanditNet fixes a Lagrange multiplier lambda and minimises IPS with shifted losses (delta_i - lambda), sweeping lambda on a grid and keeping the policy with best SNIPS on training data; lambda=0 (plain IPS) was worse than the logging policy; solutions whose control variate S lies outside about [0.974, 1.026] are discarded. P4/P5 DR: per-example doubly robust score Gamma_i(a) = mu_hat(x_i,a) + 1{a_i=a}(y_i - mu_hat(x_i,a))/e_hat(a|x_i), cross-fitted; policy maximises sum_i Gamma_i(pi(x_i)) over a restricted class (equivalently weighted classification), regret O(sqrt(VC/n)) relative to the best policy in the class. With full information (our case) Gamma_i(a) reduces to the observed outcome y_i(a), so IPS/DR add nothing at the one-step level. P6: L = alpha*[selective risk + lambda*max(0, c - coverage)^2] + (1-alpha)*L_aux, alpha=0.5, lambda=32; the auxiliary head is stated to be essential (without it the network focuses on a c-fraction before good features exist). P8 cost-sensitive surrogate (eq. 4): L~CE(g, c) = - sum_i (max_j c(j) - c(i)) * log softmax_i(g), proven consistent (Prop. 1: argmax of the minimiser equals argmin of expected cost) and convex; deferral loss (eq. 7) L_CE = -log softmax_y(g) - 1[m=y] log softmax_perp(g), consistent (Thm. 1); alpha-reweighted variant L^alpha_CE down-weights examples where the expert is right, alpha chosen on validation, with a cheaper 'fine-tune last stage' procedure in the appendix. P9: the softmax parametrisation of P8 is not calibrated w.r.t. expert correctness; a one-vs-all surrogate is consistent and calibrated. P12: offline heuristic labels from ground truth (e.g. UPDATE labelled positive if the update raises confidence on more than half of future frames) initialise and regularise Q (weighted (Q - Q_init)^2), then Q-learning on-policy with binary correct/incorrect reward every 50 frames. Ours (tracking/z13_region_value_loss.py): target = good - harm in {-1,0,+1} for each region, MSE averaged within query (1/n per action) then over queries; unknown-kind rows excluded; no explicit imbalance handling (about 5% helpful, most neutral). CONSISTENCY ANALYSIS. (1) Per-action MSE: its pointwise minimiser is f*(x,a)=E[good-harm|x,a]=P(good|x,a)-P(harm|x,a) (outcomes are exclusive). The plug-in rule 'act on argmax_a f*(x,a) iff it is > 0' is Bayes-optimal for the utility U = good - harm relative to the default; the per-query 1/n weights depend only on x and do not change the pointwise minimiser. So the REGRESSION part is Fisher-consistent for that (equal-weight) utility - this is the regression reduction of cost-sensitive classification (Vowpal Wabbit's csoaa) - but with three caveats: (a) it is consistent only for the utility encoded by the label; equal weighting of a fix and a harm and the discarding of magnitude may not match HOTA; (b) decision regret is controlled only through sup-norm/L2 accuracy of f_hat near the decision boundary (regret <= 2*max_a|f_hat-f*| pointwise); with most f* ~ 0 and helpful advantages ~0.05 in expectation, MSE is dominated by fitting neutral zeros and the required accuracy is far below the head's noise (low-margin regime); (c) argmax over n noisy estimates of near-zero advantages is biased upward (optimizer's curse, P15): with independent zero-mean noise P(max_a f_hat_a > 0) = 1 - 2^-n, so the 'z>0' rule acts in almost every query - consistent with the observed 1000-3500 selections of 4183 fit20 rows with only 13-33 outcome changes. (2) Softmax with fixed zero logit + threshold tau on probability: NOT a consistent decision rule for any tau>0. p_max = exp(z_max)/(1+sum_j exp(z_j)) depends on n and on the other candidates' scores, not only on z_max. Since regression targets are in [-1,1], even a perfect predictor (z=1 for the helpful region, 0 for others) gives p_max = e/(1+e+(n-1)): 0.73 for n=1, 0.48 for n=3, 0.32 for n=6 - which explains why the probability 'never exceeds about 0.6'. Two queries with identical advantage of the best action receive different decisions depending on how many neutral candidates are present; for tau above 1/(1+n) the rule mostly filters by the number of candidates, not by advantage. Exponentiating MSE regression outputs also mixes units (an advantage is not a log-odds). Only tau=0 reduces the rule to the consistent plug-in. (3) Selecting tau by mean per-video net effect over 20 videos and 11 grid values is itself an argmax of noisy estimates (selection bias again); the frequent choice tau=1.01 (abstain) is the honest outcome when no tau gives a reliable positive net effect. Bottom line: the loss is consistent for an equal-weight one-step utility but statistically inefficient for rare positives; the threshold rule is inconsistent; neither handles the multi-step effect of an override.
data_camera_resolution_rate: P3 BanditNet: CIFAR-10 (50k train/10k test, 32x32) converted to synthetic bandit feedback from a logging policy with about 49% error; no real logged feedback, no video. P1: multilabel text/image benchmarks converted to bandit feedback [uncertain: exact datasets not re-checked]. P5: observational social-science data (e.g. counseling/program evaluation), no vision [uncertain]. P6: CIFAR-10, SVHN, Cats vs Dogs (VGG-16 variant), Concrete Compressive Strength regression; three runs per setting. P8: synthetic Gaussian mixtures (200 trials), CIFAR-10/100 with synthetic experts (WideResNet-28), CIFAR10H, hate-speech text, CheXpert. P12: 16,384 Internet videos (~10.9M frames, ~109K binary-annotated frames, a check every 50 frames at IoU 0.5), evaluated also on OTB-2013 (50 videos), VOT-2016 (60 videos) and a held-out set of 16 long videos (>=5,000 frames each); hand-held/moving cameras typical of Internet video; single-object tracking, ~10 fps on a K40. None of P1-P11 uses video, a moving camera or MOT. Ours: BDD100K MOT, moving vehicle camera, fit84 (training) / fit20 (threshold) / train26 (evaluation) video split, 37296 queries of which 26600 have known labels; one-step labels per candidate region.
metrics_and_numbers: P3 (BanditNet, text mirror): Bandit-ResNet20 test error from about 13% down to 8.2% as logged feedback grows, approaching the full-information ResNet skyline; logging policy error about 49%; best lambda in 0.8-1.0; plain IPS (lambda=0) worse than the logging policy. P6 (SelectiveNet): Table 1 - target vs realised test coverage, e.g. target 0.75 -> softmax-response (SR) 64.16%, SelectiveNet 80.17%; average violation SR 11.98 vs SelectiveNet 3.63 points (motivates post-hoc calibration). Sec. 5 - calibrate tau as the 100(1-c) percentile of g on an unlabeled validation set, with Hoeffding guarantee epsilon = sqrt(ln(2/delta)/(2n)). Table 5 (Concrete regression) - selective MSE 27.94 vs MC-dropout 33.70 at coverage 0.70 (17.09% relative). Table 6 - calibrating to a coverage far from the trained coverage costs risk (e.g. CIFAR-10 trained c=0.70, calibrated to 0.90: 2.65% vs 2.43% for model trained at 0.90; 3 runs). P8 (learning to defer): Table 1 synthetic, L0_CE minus confidence baseline +6.39 [3.71, 9.06] system accuracy points; minus oracle +0.22 [-1.71, 2.15]; minus mixture-of-experts +2.01 [0.14, 4.06]. Sec. 6.2 CIFAR-10: L_CE beats confidence baseline by 1.01 and LearnedOracle by 1.94 points on average; with 2,000 training points 70.12% vs 62.33% (+7.89) for the confidence baseline (Fig. 4) - the gain is largest in the small-data regime; mixture-of-experts loss learns never to defer (inconsistent). Sec. 6.3 CIFAR-100: +1.60 for 30<=k<=90. P12 (tracking, F1 on held-out long videos): base FCNT online heuristics ~0.08-0.09; offline supervised one-step heuristics 0.13 (track only), 0.14 (update only), 0.20 (both); on-policy Q-learning 0.30 (update action alone 0.28); CCOT backbone 0.36. These are the authors' metrics and must not be translated into expected HOTA for our bench.
distinguishing_ablations: P3: lambda sweep shows the translation constant (i.e. what is treated as the zero/baseline value) decides success; lambda=0 fails, a REINFORCE-style learned baseline put lambda outside the good range; variance regularisation untuned; single benchmark, synthetic feedback. P6: auxiliary head declared essential (small alpha gives poor selective risk); coverage-calibration matrix (Table 6) shows a model is near-optimal only near its trained coverage; 3 runs. Independent critique P11: the advantage of SelectiveNet-type methods comes mostly from a better-generalising classifier; selecting with the classifier's own scores (softmax response on the trained model) does as well or better - i.e. a separate learned selection head is not the mandatory component. P8: consistency matters empirically - the inconsistent mixture-of-experts loss collapses to never deferring; the confidence-threshold two-model baseline (consistent but two models) loses mainly in the small-data regime (Fig. 4); alpha has 'sizable influence' and must be validated; component mandatory for the claim: a single softmax with a jointly trained deferral logit. P9: P8's softmax gives uncalibrated deferral probabilities (cannot be used as a calibrated threshold quantity) - one-vs-all fixes calibration while keeping consistency. P10: under misspecified (restricted) model classes, consistent surrogates can still fail badly; exact MILP formulations do better on small problems. P12 (tracking, the only direct decision-learning evidence): learned policy > hand-designed heuristics; offline one-step supervised labels (0.20) are clearly worse than on-policy Q-learning (0.30) - evidence that labels computed under the default's roll-in under-estimate/mis-estimate the value of an intervention; short-term-trained policy beats long-term policy on short benchmarks (over-predicts occlusion), i.e. decision policies do not transfer across horizon; performance rises with the number of training videos up to 8,000-12,000 videos - orders of magnitude more decision events than our ~100 training videos. Seeds/runs: P12 single training stream; P8 3 runs on some settings [uncertain]; P6 3 runs.
explanations_addressed: Lost discriminative/spatial info in the readout: not addressed by any source (all assume the features carry the signal); caution - P11 shows that selection quality is bounded by the underlying predictor's quality, so if the 68 pooled features do not rank helpful above neutral regions, no objective or threshold will help. Target-vs-neighbour identification: not addressed. Training objective mismatched to the final assignment: DIRECT evidence/theory - P8 Prop. 1 gives a consistent softmax surrogate for exactly our structure (K candidate actions + zero-cost default) with costs relative to the default; P5 shows directly maximising the empirical advantage over a policy class has regret guarantees, whereas per-action regression is only plug-in consistent and degrades under misspecification and low margin; our probability threshold is inconsistent (see labels_and_loss). Rare useful events with high harm cost: DIRECT design guidance - P1 variance penalty and pessimistic offline RL (P15 background) argue for acting only on a lower confidence bound of the advantage; P6/P7/P14 give coverage and risk calibration with finite-sample guarantees (Hoeffding/binomial bounds; Learn-then-Test fixed-sequence testing) on a held-out calibration split; P8 alpha reweighting is a tunable harm/benefit trade-off; the optimizer's curse (P15) explains the observed flood of neutral selections. Insufficient history: not addressed (P12 uses recurrent belief but no ablation of history). Limits of the action: caution - P12 shows one-step offline labels under-represent multi-step consequences of track/update decisions (0.20 vs 0.30 F1); P16 (DAgger) explains why: roll-in distribution shift. Our labels are exact one-step re-assignments under the baseline roll-in, so even a perfect one-step policy can mis-predict closed-loop HOTA.
evidence_strength: Theory for consistency (P8 Prop.1/Thm.1, P5 regret bounds, P2/P3 equivariance) is peer-reviewed and strong as mathematics; empirical support is moderate and entirely outside tracking (synthetic bandit conversion of CIFAR-10, CIFAR with synthetic experts, small regression sets). Independent critiques exist (P9 on calibration, P11 on selection heads, P10 on misspecification), which narrows what can be claimed. Official code: SelectiveNet and learn-to-defer repositories are cited in the papers (not opened); BanditNet code/data page exists. Tracking evidence (P12) is a single peer-reviewed ICCV paper without code, single-object, different action set. Overall: strong for 'the threshold rule is inconsistent and the cost-sensitive softmax surrogate with a default class is consistent'; weak-to-moderate for 'changing the objective will produce a measurable gain on our bench'.
difference_from_tried: What we tried: per-action MSE regression of good-minus-harm ({-1,0,+1}), argmax with fixed default logit 0, plus a softmax-probability threshold tau chosen on fit20 by mean per-video net effect; earlier fixed/learned 3-peak association, ridge target model, category replacement, context features. Differences implied by the sources: (1) objective - replace per-action independent MSE by a single listwise cost-sensitive softmax over {default, region_1..region_n} with weights (max_j c_j - c_i) (P8 eq. 4), costs c = -(good - harm) + epsilon for every non-default action (epsilon = explicit intervention cost that makes the default win ties and gives all-neutral queries a gradient toward abstaining). This changes what the head learns: relative ranking of candidates against the default within the same query, instead of an absolute regression dominated by neutral zeros. (2) decision rule - act iff margin z_best - z_default > tau on the logit scale (no softmax probability), which removes the dependence on the number of candidates; optionally a lower-confidence-bound version across seeds/folds (pessimism) against the optimizer's curse. (3) calibration - tau chosen on cross-fitted out-of-fold predictions over all 104 fit videos (84+20), using a risk-control procedure (Learn-then-Test fixed-sequence test on per-video net harm, or SelectiveNet-style coverage quantile with Hoeffding margin), never touching train26. (4) IPS/BanditNet/DR estimators are NOT needed at the one-step level because we observe every candidate's outcome; they would only add variance. They become relevant only if we later log closed-loop outcomes for a sampled action per query (then DR with known sampling propensities). If one restricts to tau=0 and keeps MSE, there is NO difference from what was tried - the regression plug-in is already the 'direct method'.
candidate_node_change: Node: FlyVis readout of activity (loss and decision rule of the region-scoring head) - a readout node of the fly path per AGENTS.md; FlyVis core/state unchanged. Change: (a) cost-sensitive listwise softmax surrogate with an explicit default class (P8 eq. 4) and intervention cost epsilon; (b) margin-on-logit decision rule replacing the softmax-probability threshold; (c) cross-fitted, risk-controlled threshold on fit videos only. Which FlyVis problem it addresses: the readout's inability to rank and abstain (the useful full-box action exists - oracle +5.24 pp [4.23; 6.25] - but the trained readout selects neutral actions and its score does not estimate advantage). Equal controls, all with identical new loss/rule/calibration and identical query UIDs: old D (same FlyVis features), stock C, eye input R1, no-fly geometry-only head; plus 'old MSE loss + new margin rule' and 'new loss + old probability rule' to separate the rule from the loss. Cheap distinguishing checks on saved data (CPU, no new FlyVis maps): (1) Zero-training re-analysis of saved logits/calibrations of z13_box_supervision_followup_v1: tabulate p_max vs number of candidates n and verify the bound e/(e+n); re-run the fit20 calibration with the margin rule z_max > tau over a grid on the logit scale; if net effect on fit20 becomes positive for D but not for geometry, the threshold was a bottleneck. (2) Ranking diagnostic on fit20 for each arm: among queries with >=1 helpful region, top-1 rate of a helpful region versus the default and versus neutral regions, and precision at fixed coverage (risk-coverage/AURC curve); compare against the base rate and against geometry. If D is not above geometry and base rate, stop: the information is missing from the readout input (objective changes cannot help) and the next item should be a feature/spatial change, not this one. (3) Retrain the 24 heads (4 arms x 3 seeds x 2 settings) with the new surrogate on fit84, 5-fold video cross-fitting for out-of-fold scores on fit84+fit20, choose tau by fixed-sequence testing (most conservative first) requiring the one-sided 95% lower bound of mean per-video (beneficial - harmful)/known > 0 on out-of-fold videos; freeze before train26. Condition to proceed: on out-of-fold fit data, D's precision among selected actions clearly above the helpful base rate and D minus geometry lower bound > 0; then a single train26 evaluation against the pre-registered criteria (D - baseline mean >= +2 pp and lower > 0; D - C, D - R1, D - geometry lower > 0). Only if train26 passes: separately budgeted closed-loop HOTA (GPU, MASA) because one-step labels can mis-predict closed-loop value (P12). No GPU stage is justified by this source alone.
strongest_objection: The observed failure is most likely a missing-signal problem, not an objective problem. Among 1000-3500 selected fit20 actions only 13-33 changed the outcome, i.e. the readout's precision for non-neutral actions is around 1%, apparently at or below the base rate of helpful candidates; consistency results (P8, P5) are statements about population minimisers over all measurable functions and say nothing about whether 68 region-pooled features plus geometry can separate helpful from neutral regions with ~100 training videos. P10 and P11 show that under restricted model classes, consistent surrogates and selection heads give little or nothing beyond the quality of the underlying scorer. In addition, labels are one-step counterfactuals under the baseline roll-in; P12 shows offline one-step labels for tracker decisions are clearly inferior to on-policy learning, so even a perfectly fitted one-step policy may not transfer to closed-loop HOTA. Finally, a risk-controlled threshold on ~100 videos with ~5% positives will often - correctly - choose to abstain, so the most likely result of a correct implementation is 'no action', i.e. 0 pp.
cost_and_hardware: CPU only for all three checks: (1) re-analysis of saved logits/calibrations - minutes; (2) ranking/risk-coverage diagnostic - minutes; (3) retraining 24 small heads with the listwise surrogate and 5-fold cross-fitting - about 5x the previous training cost per arm (previous protocol budgeted training within 1800 s per model batch), feasible on CPU with saved features in runs/z13_box_supervision_followup_20261025 (features npz per arm/split). No new FlyVis maps and no GPU are needed unless the train26 gate passes; closed-loop HOTA with MASA would then need the single 12 GB GPU under the usual one-CUDA-process rule and the author's 07:40 MSK deadline.
